Windows Graphics Capture uses the event-driven compositor cadence and a bounded frame pool, excludes the cursor, and normalizes the client to 640x360 BGRA. The GDI fallback is paced at 33 ms. Object inference observes a 4/60-second minimum interval with bounded latest-frame work. Hacker Atlas samples every eighth matched capture, and durable Game Play Atlas persistence is paced at 7.5 Hz. Native tests cover the GDI client area and cursor, motion admission, and inference cadence. Interactive compositor cadence and capture timing with the physical game remain unverified.

The platform-equivalent path is GdiWindowCapture plus FrameGeometry and CpuBgraNormalizer: client-only top-origin BGRA is center-cropped to 16:9, resampled to 640x360 and retains capture identity. Program tests cover exact/wide/tall crop, projection center and channel-preserving solid normalization; ObjectDetectionIntegrationTests verifies title-bar exclusion against real Windows windows. Windows uses raw per-channel BGRA bilinear interpolation, whereas Mac preserves Core Image color management and can fail createCGImage conversion; no pixel differential or failure-path coverage establishes equivalence. Windows tracking consumes the canonical frame directly, so a separate solveWidth result is unnecessary.

HollowKnightWindowLocator.cs ports GameWindowCandidate and GameWindowSelection with the same exact normalized-title preference followed by largest nonnegative client area among non-minimized candidates. UI Program tests map both Mac cases: gameplay beats a Unity helper, and untitled candidates fall back to largest area. Production locator uses that selection result and adds a Windows-specific minimized-last adaptation before applying the shared ordering.

Windows ports the acceptance, innovation, promotion, cadence, provisional/trusted reference, owned evidence, spatial handoff, patch matching, correction and rollback policies. GroundCameraSolverTests includes the invalid-quality acceptance and promotion guards. Additional suites cover broad recent references, long rows and motion near an edge. Accepted captures prioritize motion-admitted floor rows and retry against the intact raw reference when those rows disappear. Windows live tracking refines every accepted capture at subpixel precision and independently verifies an eligible pooled match while retaining its original quality bound. The separate broad solver retains its existing source-ranking and large-shake placement policy. Replaying King’s Pass to Dirtmouth with the Windows Host recovered ground on all 96 pre-cut frames, compared with zero before the port. That recording still lacks the edge-local measured contact needed to establish a doorway floor seam. Native gameplay comparison remains open.

GroundPatchConsensus revalidates each unique patch at the shared median displacement before reporting support or error. Direct mapped fixtures cover the moving foreground majority, ambiguity, masks, invalid bounds, and a patch that fails at the shared displacement. The Windows texture-only fallback also allows vertical spread to measure narrow walls. The solver's source ranking differs from the Mac path.

GroundComputeProcessing.cs and GroundCudaPatchMatcher.cs implement normalized patch scoring on NVIDIA CUDA, with CPU/parallel fallback, ordered results, reusable buffers, serialized dispatch and measured search telemetry. Production camera and ground-feature trackers select CUDA automatically for at least 64 candidates and allow 192-pixel recovery. GTX 1080 hardware-required tests cover score/motion parity, malformed samples, fallback, concurrent calls and buffer resizing. The installed app publishes device, dispatch count and camera backend diagnostics. Smaller image preprocessing remains CPU; an explicit GPU image backend and forced device-loss/encoder-failure tests remain absent. See GPU_TRACKING_AUDIT.md for measurements and limitations.

Tests verify source pixels, matching tracker output, rectangle conversion, and one pending write with 10 Hz admission. A photographic cross-platform data comparison remains open.

GroundDetectionEfficiencyTests, GroundReferenceDetectorParityTests, GroundEarlyRecognitionTests, GroundSurfaceEvidenceTests, GroundLinePresenceTests and mapped Program regressions cover the production detector algorithms extensively. They use the current frame’s masked edge response, semantic run evidence, and selected floors, do no image work while disabled, and default off. Ground Lines and Ground Tracking Patches are separate controls that default on. The current Mac Clean Floor Lines layer paints semantic floors directly. Pixel-by-pixel equivalence on recorded gameplay remains to be verified.
